case_title: Karthi @ Karthick v. State Rep. by Inspector of Police, Tamil Nadu
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour (both residents of Achampatti); prior acquaintance in which the accused teased the victim and asked her to marry him; later repeated sexual relations over about six months on a promise of marriage
evidence_type: Testimonial (victim, victim's brother and father); circumstantial (four village elders on the panchayat; two friends of the accused); medical examination of the victim by a doctor (findings not described in the judgment)
aggravating_circumstances: Forcible first intercourse with the mouth gagged; deception by promise of marriage used to secure silence and then repeated intercourse over about six months
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.376 and 417 by the Assistant Sessions Judge, Virudhunagar; sentence not stated in the judgment
neutral_facts: The victim, a young woman, was a neighbour of the accused in the same village. The victim had lost her mother in early childhood and lived with her brother's family, and her father also lived in the house. The accused used to tease the victim and repeatedly asked her to marry him. On one occasion the victim was alone at home while other family members were at a temple. The accused entered the house and asked for sexual intercourse. The victim refused and said intercourse could only take place after marriage. The accused gagged the victim's mouth with the accused's right hand and had sexual intercourse with the victim. Afterwards the accused told the victim not to reveal the incident to anyone, promising marriage while placing a hand on the victim's head. Over about six months the two were intimate repeatedly at different places, and the accused repeatedly said marriage would follow. During a visit to a temple, the accused refused to marry the victim. The victim told the victim's brother and father, who sought the help of village elders. The elders convened a panchayat and summoned the accused, who again refused to marry. The victim then lodged a complaint with the police on 10 October 2003. Prosecution evidence included the testimony of the victim, the victim's brother and father, four village elders who attended the panchayat, two friends of the accused who had met the victim and the accused at the temple, and a doctor who medically examined the victim.
physical_harm: No injury described in the judgment; the victim's mouth was gagged by the accused's hand during the first intercourse
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of the victim, her brother and father; statements of four village elders on the panchayat, which the court called strong circumstantial evidence; statements of two friends of the accused (PW9, PW10) confirming the promise and its withdrawal at the temple
witness_credibility: Court found the victim, her brother and father, the village elders and the two friends consistent and not discredited by cross-examination; the accused could not create any dent in the victim's testimony
post_offence_conduct: Victim disclosed the matter to family and village elders and lodged a police complaint on 10.10.2003; accused surrendered before the Judicial Magistrate on 5.11.2003
bail_history: Released on bail by the Supreme Court vide order dated 4.4.2008; no other bail history stated
trial_duration: offence: not given (complaint 10.10.2003); trial judgment: 30.11.2004; High Court: 18.12.2006; Supreme Court: 1.7.2013
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: R. Balasubrmanian, K.V. Vijayakumar, T.R.B. Siva Kumar. State/respondent: A. Yogesh Kanna, A. Santha Kumaran, B. Balaji
investigation_status: FIR/complaint registered 10.10.2003; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed; committed to Sessions Court; trial completed with 16 prosecution witnesses and 12 exhibits
appeal_history: Trial court (Assistant Sessions Judge, 30.11.2004): convicted under ss.376 and 417 IPC. Appellate court (Additional District and Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court, 1.6.2005): conviction affirmed. High Court (Madurai Bench, 18.12.2006): revision dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
defence_argument: Relationship was consensual; no promise of marriage was made; first intercourse was six months before the complaint, so the complaint is an afterthought and the delay in FIR registration creates doubt; following Uday and Zinder Ali Sheikh, each case of consent obtained by deceit must be judged on its own facts
legal_principle_applied: Consent obtained by deceit (false promise of marriage) is not a legitimate defence; a relationship during a subsisting commitment of marriage is not rape under s.376, but becomes so once the promise is refused; delay in FIR does not create doubt where the victim disclosed promptly after refusal and the village elders' panchayat intervened
precedent_relied_upon: Uday v. State of Karnataka (2003) 4 SCC 46 and Zinder Ali Sheikh v. State of West Bengal (2009) 3 SCC 761 (both referred to; relied on by the appellant's counsel)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Deceit by false promise of marriage used to secure silence and then repeated intercourse over about six months; forcible first intercourse with the victim's mouth gagged
other_sentence_order: Accused to be taken into custody to serve the remaining part of the sentence
